content: The Sloane Hospital for Women serves as the obstetrics and gynecology division within New York-Presbyterian Hospital and the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology at the Columbia University College of Physicians and Surgeons in New York City. The Sloane Maternity Hospital was established in 1886 through a donation from William D. Sloane and his wife, Emily Thorn Vanderbilt Sloane, who was the granddaughter of Cornelius Vanderbilt. It was the first hospital in New York dedicated exclusively to women's healthcare. The hospital was originally located on the campus of the College of Physicians and Surgeons (P&S) in Midtown Manhattan, at Amsterdam Avenue and 59th Street. It opened its doors in early 1888 and served as a teaching facility for P&S students. The hospital quickly gained recognition for its exceptional sanitary practices and low mortality rates. It was also the first hospital in the United States to integrate obstetrics and gynecology into a single institution. In 1910, the facility was renamed the Sloane Hospital for Women. A new surgical building, funded by the Sloane family, was added in 1911. By 1925, the hospital became part of Presbyterian Hospital, which was affiliated with P&S. In 1928, the hospital relocated to its current site on 168th Street in the Washington Heights neighborhood of northern Manhattan. At this location, it retained its branding while occupying several floors of the Presbyterian Hospital building. As both a research and clinical institution, the Sloane Hospital for Women has been at the forefront of numerous advancements in the field of obstetrics and gynecology. These include the development of the Apgar score, the introduction of RhoGAM, and the use of amniocentesis.
